root_cause:
AnsiDecoder.decode split its input with str.splitlines(), which drops the final empty segment, so a trailing newline vanished: Text.from_ansi('text
') gave 'text' and Text.from_ansi('
') gave '' (issue #3577: Text('
') != Text.from_ansi('
')). from_ansi joins the decoded lines with '
', so the lost last segment meant the lost trailing newline.
best_solution:
In rich/ansi.py AnsiDecoder.decode, replace `for line in terminal_text.splitlines(): yield self.decode_line(line)` with `for line in re.split(r"(?<=
)", terminal_text): yield self.decode_line(line.rstrip("
"))`. Splitting after each '
' keeps a final empty segment when the text ends in a newline, so decode yields one more (empty) Text and Text.from_ansi's '
'-join puts the newline back exactly. '' -> [''] -> '', '
' -> ['', ''] -> '
', 'a

' -> ['a','',''] -> 'a

'. The fix has to go in decode() itself, not in from_ansi, because a test checks decode()'s list output directly.

locating_signals: The statement is only the PR title 'preserve newlines' plus a link to issue #3577. It names no function or file. The deciding details (Text.from_ansi, trailing newline) are only in the linked issue, which the agent cannot see offline. From the statement alone, the only route is to grep for newline-dropping operations (splitlines(), rstrip('\n')) and pick the generic text-parsing path. tests/test_ansi.py already has issue-referenced regression tests (#2688), which hint at the area.
our_outcome_summary:
Failed in all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass all false). v4 and v8 (393 chars, identical) removed `.rstrip("
")` from rich/pretty.py _ipy_display_hook, which is the IPython repr path and unrelated to ANSI decoding. v6 changed the Markdown softbreak handling in rich/markdown.py to emit '
' instead of ' ', a behaviour change unrelated to the issue. v7 made no patch (109 calls, 0 chars). None touched rich/ansi.py, so 4 tests in tests/test_ansi.py still fail (test_decode, test_decode_example, test_decode_issue_2688[...], test_decode_newlines: from_ansi('
').plain == '').
generalizable_lesson:
When the statement is only a short title plus an issue link you cannot open, turn the title's verb into a grep for the code operations that break it ("preserve newlines" -> splitlines(), rstrip('
'), strip(), split('
')). Rank the matches by how general and public-facing the path is: parsing and conversion helpers like from_*/decode/parse come before display hooks or niche renderers. Then confirm the candidate with a round-trip repro (f(x) == x for '', '
', 'a
', '
a', 'a

') before editing, and do not change unrelated behaviour such as Markdown softbreaks to fit a vague title. Remember that str.splitlines() silently drops a trailing empty line and also splits on , \v,   and \x1c-\x1e. When newlines must survive a split and re-join, use re.split(r'(?<=
)', s) or s.split('
').
acceptable_alternatives:
Any change in AnsiDecoder.decode that yields one extra empty Text when the input ends in '
' (for example `terminal_text.split('
')` followed by decode_line on each part, or splitlines() plus appending Text('') when terminal_text.endswith('
')). A fix only in Text.from_ansi (appending '
') would pass test_decode_newlines and test_decode_issue_2688 but fail test_decode, which checks decode()'s output list directly.
